core_obligations: First proof (proof lines 12870-12873): combine the characterisation of perfect objects through pseudo-coherence and locally finite tor dimension with the triangle lemmas for pseudo-coherence and for tor amplitude; choosing which two of the three objects are assumed perfect selects the appropriate parts of those triangle lemmas.

Second proof, reduce locally (proof lines 12874-12880): suppose K and L are perfect; for an object U one passes to a covering over which K|U and L|U are represented by strictly perfect complexes K^bullet and L^bullet, and then to a further covering over which the map K|U -> L|U is given by a map of complexes alpha (by the local representability lemma).
Conclude the second proof (proof lines 12881-12883): M|U is then isomorphic to the cone of alpha, which is strictly perfect by the cone lemma, and since this holds locally M is perfect.
proof_roadmap: For the first proof, combine the perfect-object characterisation with the two triangle lemmas.
For the second proof, reduce to strictly perfect representatives of two of the objects on a covering and represent the map by a map of complexes.
Identify the third object with the cone of that map and use strict perfectness of cones.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that perfection is a two-out-of-three property for distinguished triangles (statement lines 12862-12867). The author gives two proofs (proof lines 12869-12883): the first combines the characterisation of perfect objects with the triangle lemmas for pseudo-coherence and for tor amplitude, and the second is a construction — reduce to strictly perfect representatives of two objects on a covering, represent the connecting map by a map of complexes, and identify the third object with the cone, strictly perfect by the cone lemma. H2: two independent short arguments, both written out.
